# std.dp

The DP toolkit: the structures and optimizations a DP calls by name (CHT, SOS; a 0/1 knapsack over sums is `Bitset.shift_or`).  A minimum or maximum of lines (the convex hull trick) is a `LiChao`; a layer whose optimal split moves right is `dnc_layer` (over `monotone_minima`); an interval DP with monotone splits is `knuth`; "exactly `k` pieces" over a convex cost is `aliens`. Meet in the middle starts from `subset_sums`; sums over subsets and supersets of masks are `std.ntt`'s `sos(mut f, over: Sub | Sup = Sub, inverse:)`. The recurrence itself stays in your code, and a memoized recursion is `@memo`. Each optimization names the law it needs; `std.spec` checks it on small inputs (`monge_break`, `dnc_break`, `knuth_break`, `convexity_break`). A sliding-window optimum is `a.window_fold(k, op)` or `std.window.Window(op)`.

In prelude (no `use` needed): `LiChao`, `Line`, `LineContainer`, `MonotoneHull`, `Step`, `aliens`, `backtrack`, `knuth`, `monge_path`, `monotone_minima`, `smawk`.

## `struct Line(pub k: Int, pub m: Int)`

\(O(1)\) per evaluation.

- `fn at(self, x: Int) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); Evaluate the line at `x`: `k * x + m`.; traps: when `k * x + m` overflows `Int`

## `struct LiChao<L = Line, K = Int>(pick: (K, K) -> K, lo: Int, hi: Int)`

\(O(\log n)\) per `at`, \(O(\log n)\) per whole-line `add`, \(O(\log^2 n)\) on a segment.

Fields: `lines: List<?L>`, `left: List<Int>`, `right: List<Int>`.

- `fn new(pick: (K, K) -> K, over: Range<Int>) -> LiChao<L, K>` — \(O(1)\); An empty envelope over the integer coordinates `over`, keeping at each `x` the value `pick` prefers (`min` for the lower envelope, `max` for the upper).; traps: when `over` is empty
- `fn clear(mut self)` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Forget every line, keeping `pick` and `over`, so the tree can be reused (between test cases, say) without reallocating.
- `fn at(self, x: Int) -> ?K` — \(O(\log n)\) for n = `over.len`; The best value at `x` over every line covering `x`, as chosen by `pick`, or `None` when no line covers `x` (nothing added yet, or only segments that miss `x`).; traps: when `x` is not in `over`
- `fn line_at(self, x: Int) -> ?L` — \(O(\log n)\) for n = `over.len`; The line attaining `at(x)`, or `None` when no line covers `x`.; traps: when `x` is not in `over`
- `fn add(mut self, line: L, on: ?Range<Int> = None)` — \(O(\log n)\) for a whole line, \(O(\log^2 n)\) on a segment, for n = `over.len`; at most one new cell per level; Add `line` on every coordinate of `over`, or only on the coordinates of `on` (`on: lo..=hi`).; traps: when `on` reaches outside `over`

## `struct MongePath<N, K: Add>(nodes: List<N>, cost: (N, N) -> K)`

\(O(1)\) per step; the next cut's optimum after \(O(1)\) amortized calls of `cost`.

- `fn next(mut self) -> (val: K, prev: Int)` — \(O(1)\) amortized calls of `cost`; Reach the next node: return the optimum at node `len` and the index of the node before it, then grow `len` by one.; traps: when every node has been reached (`len == nodes.len`)
- `fn val(self, i: Int) -> K` — \(O(1)\); The optimum at node `i`, which must already be reached; `val(0)` is 0.; traps: when `i < 0` or `i >= len`
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of nodes reached so far, `nodes.first` included, so a fresh `MongePath` has `len == 1`.
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Never: the first node is reached before any `next()`.
- `@get fn items(self) -> yields (Int, K)` — \(O(\mathit{len})\)

## `struct MonotoneHull<P>(pick: (Int, Int) -> Int = min)`

\(O(1)\) amortized per `add` and per `at_next`, \(O(\log n)\) per `at`.

- `fn add(mut self, line: Line, tag: P = ())` — \(O(1)\) amortized; Add `line`, with `tag`.; traps: when the slope goes back
- `fn best_next(mut self, x: Int) -> ?(val: Int, tag: P)` — \(O(1)\) amortized; The best value at `x` with the tag of the line attaining it, for an `x` that never decreases between calls (a pointer walks the hull).; traps: when `x` is less than the previous `best_next` or `at_next` argument
- `fn at(self, x: Int) -> ?Int` — \(O(\log n)\); The best value at any `x`, by binary search on the hull; `None` when empty.
- `fn at_next(mut self, x: Int) -> ?Int` — \(O(1)\) amortized; `at(x)` for an `x` that never decreases between calls; `None` when empty.; traps: when `x` is less than the previous `best_next` or `at_next` argument
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of lines kept on the hull (dominated lines are not counted).
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether the hull has no line.
- `@get fn items(self) -> yields (Line, P)` — \(O(\mathit{len})\)
- `fn clear(mut self)` — \(O(1)\); Remove every line and reset the `at_next` pointer, keeping `pick`.

## `struct LineContainer(pick: (Int, Int) -> Int = min)`

\(O(\log n)\) amortized per `add`, \(O(\log n)\) per `at`.

- `fn add(mut self, line: Line)` — \(O(\log n)\) amortized; Add `line`; slopes may arrive in any order.
- `fn at(self, x: Int) -> ?Int` — \(O(\log n)\); The best value at `x`, or `None` when empty.
- `fn line_at(self, x: Int) -> ?Line` — \(O(\log n)\); The line attaining `at(x)`, or `None` when empty.
- `@get fn len(self) -> Int` — \(O(1)\); The number of lines kept (dominated lines are not counted).
- `@get fn is_empty(self) -> Bool` — \(O(1)\); Whether no line is kept.
- `fn each(self) -> yields Line` — \(O(\mathit{len})\)

## `struct Step<S>(pub state: S, pub depth: Int, pruned: Bool = false)`

One state reached by `backtrack`.

- `fn prune(mut self)` — \(O(1)\); Skip every state below this one: `backtrack` does not call `next` on it.

## Functions

- `fn monotone_minima(rows: Int, cols: Int, f: (Int, Int) -> ?Int) -> List<?(val: Int, at: Int)>` — \(O((\mathit{rows} + \mathit{cols}) \log \mathit{rows})\) calls of `f`, \(O(\mathit{rows})\) memory; For each row of the implicit `rows` x `cols` matrix `f`, the least `f(row, col)` and its leftmost `col`, or `None` where `f` is `None` on the whole row.; traps: when `rows < 0` or `cols < 0`
- `fn dnc_layer(prev: List<?Int>, cost: (Int, Int) -> Int) -> List<?Int>` — \(O(n \log n)\) calls of `cost` for n = `prev.len`; One layer of a partition DP: `next[i]` is the least `prev[j] + cost(j, i)` over `j < i` with `prev[j]` present, or `None` when no such `j` exists, so `next[0]` is always `None`.
- `fn knuth(n: Int, cost: (Int, Int) -> Int) -> List<List<Int>>` — \(O(n^2)\) time, memory and calls of `cost`; The interval DP over cuts `0..=n`: `dp[i][i + 1] = 0` and `dp[i][j] = cost(i, j) + min over i < k < j of dp[i][k] + dp[k][j]`, returned as the full `(n + 1) x (n + 1)` table.; traps: when `n < 0`
- `fn aliens<L: Add + Sub + Mul>(k: Int, solve: L -> (val: L, count: Int), lambdas: ?Range<L> = None) -> L` — \(O(\log \mathit{lambdas}.\mathit{len})\) calls of `solve` (fewer once a count is exactly `k`); \(O(\log \lvert λ \cdot \rvert)\) more without `lambdas`; `f(k)` for a convex `f` known only through its penalized form: `solve(λ)` returns the least `f(c) + λ * c` over every count `c`, and the least `c` attaining it.; traps: when `k < 0`, when `lambdas` is empty, or when no `λ` in `lambdas` gives a count of at most `k`
- `fn subset_sums(xs: List<Int>) -> List<Int>` — \(O(2^n)\) time and memory for n = `xs.len`; Every subset sum of `xs`, one per subset (repeats kept), sorted ascending: the half of a meet-in-the-middle.; traps: when a sum overflows `Int`
- `fn monge_path<N, K>(nodes: List<N>, cost: (N, N) -> K) -> (val: K, count: Int)` — \(O(n)\) calls of `cost` (online LARSCH), \(O(n)\) memory, for n = `nodes.len`; The shortest path from `nodes.first` to `nodes.last` along increasing edges `nodes[j] -> nodes[i]`, `j < i`, of weight `cost(nodes[j], nodes[i])`: its total and its number of edges.; traps: when `nodes` is empty
- `fn monge_paths<N, K>(nodes: List<N>, cost: (N, N) -> K) -> (val: List<K>, prev: List<Int>)` — \(O(n)\) calls of `cost` (online LARSCH), \(O(n)\) memory, for n = `nodes.len`; Every shortest path from `nodes.first`: `val[i]` is the least total weight to `nodes[i]` and `prev[i]` the index before it on that path (`val[0] == 0`, `prev[0] == 0`).; traps: when `nodes` is empty
- `fn smawk(rows: Int, cols: Int, f: (Int, Int) -> Int) -> List<(val: Int, at: Int)>` — \(O(\mathit{rows} + \mathit{cols})\) calls of `f`; For each row of the implicit `rows` x `cols` matrix `f`, the least `f(row, col)` and its leftmost `col`.; traps: when `rows < 0`, or `cols <= 0` with `rows > 0`
- `fn lis_ends<D, T, K>(self: [D]T, strict: Bool = true, by: T -> K = x => x) -> [D]Int` — \(O(n \log n)\) time, \(O(n)\) memory, one `by` call per element; The length of the longest increasing subsequence ending at each position, compared by `by`; `strict: false` allows equal neighbours (non-decreasing).
- `fn supermasks(m: Int, bits: Int) -> yields Int` — \(O(2^(\mathit{bits} - \mathit{popcount}(m)))\); Every mask of `bits` bits containing `m`, increasing from `m` to `2^bits - 1`.; traps: when `bits < 0` or `m` is not in `0..2^bits`
- `fn masks_of_size(bits: Int, k: Int) -> yields Int` — \(O(C(\mathit{bits}, k))\); Every mask of `bits` bits with exactly `k` bits set, increasing (Gosper's hack).; traps: when `bits < 0` or `k < 0`
- `fn subset_folds<T, M>(xs: List<T>, op: M) -> List<T>` — \(O(2^n)\) time and memory, one `op` call per non-empty mask, for n = `xs.len`; `out[mask]` is the fold under `op` of `xs[i]` for `i` in `mask`, in increasing `i`; `out[0]` is `op`'s identity (W10).
- `fn backtrack<S>(start: S, next: S -> yields S) -> yields Step<S>` — \(O(\mathit{visited})\) steps plus the cost of `next`; Depth-first backtracking from `start`, where `next(s)` yields the states one step on.

## Example

```cp
var lc = LiChao<Line, Int>(min, 0..=10)
lc.add(Line(2, 1))
lc.add(Line(1, 5))
print(lc.at(1)!, lc.at(10)!)
// output: 3 15
```
